body.p: The BBC published on 20 November 2026 that the Health and Safety Executive has said it is working urgently to help make the site of a partial building collapse safe. An apartment block under construction on the A4260 Cherwell Street in Banbury partly collapsed alongside scaffolding on 21 October. Thames Valley Police reported nine workers on site at the time, with two taken to hospital. A local councillor had accused HSE of holding the town to ransom over delays in the clear-up. An HSE spokesperson responded that it was “working urgently with the contractors on site as they seek to make it safe”, that the road closure is a matter for the local council, and that HSE realises this is a difficult situation for residents and businesses. Cherwell District Council’s inspectors had found the building presented a significant risk of further structural failure. Protective fencing was installed to mitigate the risk of falling debris. The lanes furthest from the site are open; those closer remain closed until the site is made safe. No published statement establishes the cause of the original collapse.

A partial collapse of a building under construction and its scaffolding leaves a residual risk of further failure. The works required to make the site safe — temporary support, exclusion, controlled dismantling or stabilisation — are temporary works. They must be managed under the project temporary works procedure and BS 5975-1:2024. CDM 2015 Regulation 19 requires that all practicable steps are taken to ensure that any new or existing structure does not collapse if, due to the carrying out of construction work, it may become unstable or is in a temporary state of weakness or instability. Any temporary support must be designed, installed and maintained to withstand foreseeable loads and used only for the purpose for which it was designed. HSE’s investigation and its advice to the contractor sit alongside, not instead of, the principal contractor’s duties to plan, manage and monitor the work and to appoint a competent Temporary Works Coordinator where required. Public interface and exclusion zones remain part of that control until the permanent condition is restored and accepted.

ul: Treat all making-safe works (propping, bracing, exclusion fencing, controlled removal) as temporary works items on the Temporary Works Register. Provisional category only — to be confirmed under the project procedure; escalate where residual collapse risk, public interface or incomplete structure are present.

Require a design brief that records the current condition of the structure and scaffold, residual risks identified by inspection, loads the temporary supports must carry, exclusion zones, sequence of works and the criteria for acceptance before any reduction in exclusion.
Do not rely on an earlier design or inspection once the structure has changed. A post-collapse condition needs a fresh assessment of load path and stability.
Coordinate with the local authorities on public exclusion and road management, but do not treat a highway decision as a substitute for a competent temporary works acceptance.
Hold points for inspection after any temporary support is installed and before any further loading, dismantling or public access is restored.
Close the temporary works item only when the structure has been verified as stable without the temporary measures, or when the measures have been formally accepted as the residual control.
